newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Rand, Dow seen buoying S.African shares next week.
newsitem.headline: Rand, Dow seen buoying S.African shares next week.

text.p: South African industrial shares were seen firm next week as upbeat local factors and expected gains on Wall Street inspired positive sentiment in the local market.
Although a ray of light shone through gold shares late this week as bullion recovered $6 rising from below the $337 per ounce level, analysts and dealers remained cautious of metal stocks.
"The positive sentiment and trend should continue next week. Wall Street has been continuing to firm," said James Scott, equity marketing manager at Societe General Frankel Pollak.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average on Thursday broke through the 7,000 level for the first time, continuing its record-breaking run.

But some analysts cautioned that the correlation between the Dow and the Johannesburg Stock Exchange's industrial index had weakened. The South African index was on Friday down some 40 points at 1245 GMT despite the Dow's surge.
"Wall Street has carried on to new highs in every session and some of it should wash into the South African market," Grahame Graham-Parker, general manager at Infinity Asset Management told Reuters.
This week has been characterised by a flood of positive reports which were seen boosting shares further next week.
Finance Minister Trevor Manuel's announcement that the government was on track to achieve a deficit of 5.1 percent of gross domestic product was well received by financial markets.
Dealers said the markets, some of which were initially sceptical of Manuel's appointment, were gaining confidence in him and that he had "come of age".
Bonds have rallied this week with rates falling around 25 points showing a return to the market by both foreign and local players.
Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals' comments that interest rates might be cut later rather than sooner disappointed briefly but stocks soon resumed their upward run.
However, portfolio managers remained cautious of gold shares despite bullion's rise to above the $342 late this week.
"There is still nervousness on gold. Fundamentally there is not a lot out there to suggest runaway prices. World inflation is still contained," Graham-Parker said.
Looking further ahead, players said the whole market was looking to the budget on March 12 for more direction although no fireworks were expected.
"We will wait until the budget, the fiscal picture looks good...There will be something but definitely not big," Matt Brenzel, portfolio manager at Coronation Asset Management said.
Next week the stock market would look to a host of company results notably from construction firms, including Grinacon, which was unbundled from the Grinaker group, Group Five and LTA Ltd.

It can also look to the January trade figures due from Tuesday which were expected to be bullish. The consensus of analysts polled by Reuters was for a 817 million rand surplus with the range between 500 million and one billion rand.
